![Invoice Ninja](https://invoicing.co/images/new_logo.png)

## Introduction
Welcome to the Invoice Ninja API documentation, your comprehensive guide to integrating Invoice Ninja's powerful features into your applications. Whether you're building a custom client, automating workflows, or integrating with other systems, our API provides the tools you need to streamline your invoicing and billing processes.

---

### What is Invoice Ninja?
Invoice Ninja is a robust source-available platform designed to simplify invoicing, billing, and payment management for freelancers, small businesses, and enterprises alike. With a user-friendly interface, customizable templates, and a suite of powerful features, Invoice Ninja empowers businesses to create professional invoices, track expenses, manage clients, and get paid faster.

---

### Client Libraries
PHP SDK can be found [here](https://github.com/invoiceninja/sdk-php)
Go SDK can be found [here](https://github.com/AshkanYarmoradi/go-invoice-ninja)

---

### Why use the Invoice Ninja API?
The Invoice Ninja API allows developers to extend the functionality of Invoice Ninja by programmatically accessing and manipulating data within their Invoice Ninja accounts. With the API, you can automate repetitive tasks, integrate with third-party services, and build custom solutions tailored to your specific business needs.

---

### Getting Started
To get started with the Invoice Ninja API, you'll need an active Invoice Ninja account (or your own self hosted installation) and API credentials. If you haven't already done so, sign up for an account at Invoice Ninja and generate your API keys from the settings section.

Once you have your API credentials, you can start exploring the API endpoints, authentication methods, request and response formats, and more using the documentation provided here.

---

### Explore the Documentation  
This documentation is organized into sections to help you navigate and understand the various aspects of the Invoice Ninja API:

- Authentication: Learn how to authenticate your requests to the API using API tokens.
- Endpoints: Explore the available API endpoints for managing invoices, clients, payments, expenses, and more.
- Request and Response Formats: Understand the structure of API requests and responses, including parameters, headers, and payloads.
- Error Handling: Learn about error codes, status messages, and best practices for handling errors gracefully.
- Code Examples: Find code examples and tutorials to help you get started with integrating the Invoice Ninja API into your applications.      

---

### Need Help?     

If you have any questions, encounter any issues, or need assistance with using the Invoice Ninja API, don't hesitate to reach out to our support team or join our community forums. We're here to help you succeed with Invoice Ninja and make the most of our API.    

Let's start building together!

---

### Authentication:

Invoice Ninja uses API tokens to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in Settings > Account Management > Integrations > API tokens

API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made to HTTP will fail.

---

### Errors:

Invoice Ninja uses standard HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of a request. below is a table of standard status codes and responses

| Status Code | Explanation                                                                 |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 200         | OK: The request has succeeded. The information returned with the response is dependent on the method used in the request. |
| 301         | Moved Permanently: This and all future requests should be directed to the given URI. |
| 303         | See Other: The response to the request can be found under another URI using the GET method. |
| 400         | Bad Request: The server cannot or will not process the request due to an apparent client error. |
| 401         | Unauthorized: Similar to 403 Forbidden, but specifically for use when authentication is required and has failed or has not yet been provided. |
| 403         | Forbidden: The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. |
| 404         | Not Found: The requested resource could not be found but may be available in the future. |
| 405         | Method Not Allowed: A request method is not supported for the requested resource. |
| 409         | Conflict: Indicates that the request could not be processed because of conflict in the request. |
| 422         | Unprocessable Entity: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors. |
| 429         | Too Many Requests: The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ("rate limiting"). |
| 500         | Internal Server Error: A generic error message, given when an unexpected condition was encountered and no more specific message is suitable. |

---

### Pagination

When using index routes to retrieve lists of data, by default we limit the number of records returned to 20. You can using standard pagination to paginate results, ie: ?per_page=50

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-auth">auth</h1>

Attempts to authenticate with the API using a email/password combination.

After authenticating with the API, the returned object is a CompanyUser object which is a bridge linking the user to the company.

The company user object contains the users permissions (admin/owner or fine grained permissions) You will most likely want to
  also include in the response of this object both the company and the user object, this can be done by using the include parameter.

```html
/api/v1/login?include=company,user
```


## Login

<a id="opIdpostLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "email": "demo@invoiceninja.com",
    "password": "Password0",
    "one_time_password": "123456",
    "passkey_challenge_token": "f8f0cf1f4f6c4de5b6d6c5d4a0f8e5b2b89e1f1a",
    "passkey_authentication": {}
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/login`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "demo@invoiceninja.com",
  "password": "Password0",
  "one_time_password": "123456",
  "passkey_challenge_token": "f8f0cf1f4f6c4de5b6d6c5d4a0f8e5b2b89e1f1a",
  "passkey_authentication": {}
}
```

<h3 id="login-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-SECRET|header|string|false|The API secret as defined by the .env variable API_SECRET. Only needed for self hosted users, and only applicable on the login route.|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relations of the CompanyUser object, format is comma separated.    <br><br><br /><br><br>> ### **Note**: it is possible to chain multiple includes together, ie. include=account,token<br><br><br /><br><br>```html<br><br>Available includes:<br><br>  user<br>  company<br>  token<br>  account<br>```<br>|
|include_static|query|string|false|This include will return the full set of static variables used in the application including:<br>  - Currencies<br>  - Countries <br>  - Languages<br>  - Payment Types<br>  - Email Templatees<br>  - Industries<br>|
|clear_cache|query|string|false|Clears cache<br><br>Clears (and rebuilds) the static variable cache.  <br>|
|body|body|object|true|User credentials<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "email" : "fred@flintstonze.com",<br>  "password" : "magicpassword123",<br>  "one_time_password" : "12345",<br>}<br>```<br>|
|» email|body|string|true|The users email address.|
|» password|body|string|false|The user password. Optional when performing passkey passwordless login.|
|» one_time_password|body|string|false|The one time password if 2FA is enabled|
|» passkey_challenge_token|body|string|false|Challenge token returned by passkey login options or second-factor challenge.|
|» passkey_authentication|body|object|false|WebAuthn assertion payload.|

<h3 id="login-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the company user object|[CompanyUser](#schemacompanyuser)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-clients">clients</h1>

The Clients API provides endpoints for managing client records within your company. A client represents a customer
or business entity that you provide services or products to.

### Key Features
- Create, read, update, and delete client records
- Manage client contact information and billing details
- View client-specific transaction history
- Handle multiple contacts per client
- Track client-specific settings and preferences

### Client Statuses
- Active: Client is currently active and can be billed
- Archived: Client is archived and hidden from active lists
- Deleted: Client is marked for deletion but retained in the database

### Best Practices
- Always validate client email addresses
- Use unique client numbers for easy reference
- Keep contact information up to date
- Set appropriate client-specific currency and tax settings


## List clients

<a id="opIdgetClients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/clients`

###  GET /api/v1/clients  
When retrieving a list of clients you can also chain query parameters in order to filter the dataset that is returned. For example, you can send a request to the following URL to retrieve clients that have a balance greater than 1000
  
```
/api/v1/clients?balance=gt:1000
``` 

You can also sort the results by adding a sort parameter. The following example will sort the results by the client name in descending order

```
/api/v1/clients?sort=name|desc
```

You can also combine multiple filters together. The following example will return clients that have a balance greater than 1000 and are not deleted and have a name that starts with "Bob"

```
/api/v1/clients?balance=gt:1000&name=Bob
```

If you wish to retrieve child relations, you can also combine the query parameter `?include=` with a comma separated list of relationships

```
/api/v1/clients?include=activities,ledger,system_logs'
```

The per_page and page variables allow pagination of the list of clients. The following example will return the second page of clients with 15 clients per page

```
/api/v1/clients?per_page=15&page=2
```

The default per_page value is 20.


<h3 id="list-clients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — pass one argument, for example `sort=id\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — chain ordering with repeated `sort[]` keys. The first is the main sort, the next breaks ties, and so on, for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=number\|asc`.<br><br>For clients, the API honors `clients` columns (such as `name`, `balance`, `number`), natural ordering for `number`, plus `contacts`, `contact_email`, and `name` / `display_name` (display name is normalized to `name`). Values that are not supported are ignored.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the entity based on their status. ie active / archived / deleted. Format is a comma separated string with any of the following options:  <br>- active<br>- archived<br>- deleted  <br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?status=archived,deleted<br>Returns only archived and deleted invoices<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by client name  <br><br>```html<br>?name=bob<br>```<br>|
|balance|query|string|false|Filter by client balance, format uses an operator and value separated by a colon. lt,lte, gt, gte, eq<br><br>```html<br>?balance=lt:10<br>```<br><br>ie all clients whose balance is less than 10<br>|
|between_balance|query|string|false|Filter between client balances, format uses two values separated by a colon<br><br>```html<br>?between_balance=10:100<br>```<br>|
|email|query|string|false|Filter by client email<br><br>```html<br>?email=jane.doe@acme.com<br>```<br>|
|id_number|query|string|false|Filter by client id_number<br><br>```html<br>?id_number=ACME-0001<br>```<br>|
|number|query|string|false|Filter by client number<br><br>```html<br>?number=0002<br>```<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Broad filter which targets multiple client columns:<br>  <br>  ```html<br>    name, <br>    id_number, <br>    contact.first_name <br>    contact.last_name, <br>    contact.email, <br>    contact.phone<br>    custom_value1,<br>    custom_value2,<br>    custom_value3,<br>    custom_value4,<br>  ```<br><br>  ```html<br>  ?filter=Bobby<br>  ```<br>|
|group|query|string|false|Returns the list of clients assigned to {group_id}<br><br>```html<br>  ?group=Wpmbk5ezJn<br>```<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Returns the list of clients with {client_id} - proxy call to retrieve a client_id wrapped in an array<br><br>```html<br>  ?client_id=Opnel5aKBz<br>```<br>|

```json

  "errors": {
    "value": [

    ]
```

```json
{
```

```json
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "message": "Unexpected error",
  "code": 500
}
```

<h3 id="list-clients-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A list of clients|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-clients-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[Client](#schemaclient)]|false|none|none|
|meta|[Meta](#schemameta)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

##  POST /api/v1/clients  
Adds a client to a company
  
> 🚨 Important    
When creating (or updating) a client you must include the child contacts with all mutating requests. Client contacts cannot be modified in isolation.

<h3 id="create-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|body|body|[ClientRequest](#schemaclientrequest)|true|none|
|» contacts|body|[[ClientContactRequest](#schemaclientcontactrequest)]|true|A list of contacts associated with the client|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the client company or organization|
|» website|body|string|false|The website URL of the client company or organization|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Notes that are only visible to the user who created the client|
|» industry_id|body|number|false|The unique identifier of the industry the client operates in|
|» size_id|body|number|false|The unique identifier for the size category of the client company or organization|
|» address1|body|string|false|First line of the client's address|
|» address2|body|string|false|Second line of the client's address, if needed|
|» city|body|string|false|The city the client is located in|
|» state|body|string|false|The state, province, or locality the client is located in|
|» postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code or ZIP code of the client|
|» phone|body|string|false|The client's phone number|
|» country_id|body|[CountryType](#schemacountrytype)|true|The unique identifier of the client's country expressed by the countries ISO number.<br><br>Optionally, instead of the country_id you can pass either the iso_3166_2 or iso_3166_3 country code into the country_code property.<br>|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» vat_number|body|string|false|The client's VAT (Value Added Tax) number, if applicable|
|» id_number|body|string|false|A unique identification number for the client, such as a tax ID or business registration number|
|» number|body|string|false|A system-assigned unique number for the client, typically used for invoicing purposes|
|» shipping_address1|body|string|false|First line of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_address2|body|string|false|Second line of the client's shipping address, if needed|
|» shipping_city|body|string|false|The city of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_state|body|string|false|The state, province, or locality of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code or ZIP code of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_country_id|body|number(integer)|false|The unique identifier of the client's shipping country expressed by the countries ISO number.<br><br>Optionally, instead of the shipping_country_id you can pass either the iso_3166_2 or iso_3166_3 country code into the shipping_country_code property.<br>|
|» group_settings_id|body|string|false|The group settings assigned to the client|
|» routing_id|body|string|false|The routing address id for e-invoicing for this client|
|» is_tax_exempt|body|boolean|false|Flag which defines if the client is exempt from taxes|
|» has_valid_vat_number|body|boolean|false|Flag which defines if the client has a valid VAT number|
|» classification|body|string|false|The classification of the client|
|» settings|body|[ClientSettings](#schemaclientsettings)|false|none|

<h3 id="create-client-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the saved client object|[Client](#schemaclient)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

##  GET /api/v1/clients/{id}

Displays a client by id


<h3 id="show-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|

<h3 id="show-client-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the client object|[Client](#schemaclient)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

##  PUT /api/v1/clients/{id}

Handles the updating of a client by id

> 🚨 Important    
When creating (or updating) a client you must include the child contacts with all mutating requests. Client contacts cannot be modified in isolation.

<h3 id="update-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Client Hashed ID|
|body|body|[ClientRequest](#schemaclientrequest)|true|Client object that needs to be updated|
|» contacts|body|[[ClientContactRequest](#schemaclientcontactrequest)]|true|A list of contacts associated with the client|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the client company or organization|
|» website|body|string|false|The website URL of the client company or organization|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Notes that are only visible to the user who created the client|
|» industry_id|body|number|false|The unique identifier of the industry the client operates in|
|» size_id|body|number|false|The unique identifier for the size category of the client company or organization|
|» address1|body|string|false|First line of the client's address|
|» address2|body|string|false|Second line of the client's address, if needed|
|» city|body|string|false|The city the client is located in|
|» state|body|string|false|The state, province, or locality the client is located in|
|» postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code or ZIP code of the client|
|» phone|body|string|false|The client's phone number|
|» country_id|body|[CountryType](#schemacountrytype)|true|The unique identifier of the client's country expressed by the countries ISO number.<br><br>Optionally, instead of the country_id you can pass either the iso_3166_2 or iso_3166_3 country code into the country_code property.<br>|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|A custom field for storing additional information|
|» vat_number|body|string|false|The client's VAT (Value Added Tax) number, if applicable|
|» id_number|body|string|false|A unique identification number for the client, such as a tax ID or business registration number|
|» number|body|string|false|A system-assigned unique number for the client, typically used for invoicing purposes|
|» shipping_address1|body|string|false|First line of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_address2|body|string|false|Second line of the client's shipping address, if needed|
|» shipping_city|body|string|false|The city of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_state|body|string|false|The state, province, or locality of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code or ZIP code of the client's shipping address|
|» shipping_country_id|body|number(integer)|false|The unique identifier of the client's shipping country expressed by the countries ISO number.<br><br>Optionally, instead of the shipping_country_id you can pass either the iso_3166_2 or iso_3166_3 country code into the shipping_country_code property.<br>|
|» group_settings_id|body|string|false|The group settings assigned to the client|
|» routing_id|body|string|false|The routing address id for e-invoicing for this client|
|» is_tax_exempt|body|boolean|false|Flag which defines if the client is exempt from taxes|
|» has_valid_vat_number|body|boolean|false|Flag which defines if the client has a valid VAT number|
|» classification|body|string|false|The classification of the client|
|» settings|body|[ClientSettings](#schemaclientsettings)|false|none|

## Delete client

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/clients/{id}`

##  DELETE /api/v1/clients/{id}

Handles the deletion of a client by id

> ❗ Note
Deleting a client does not purge the client from the system. The delete action will remove the clients data from all 
views in the application but keep it on file in case it needs to be restored.

A Client can be later restored reversing this action.  

To permanently wipe a client and all of their records from the system, use the [/purge route](/#tag/clients/POST/api/v1/clients/{id}/purge)


<h3 id="delete-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Client Hashed ID|

<h3 id="blank-client-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A blank client object|[Client](#schemaclient)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

## Bulk client actions

<a id="opIdbulkClients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/clients/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "action": "archive",
    "ids": [
      "2J234DFA,D2J234DFA,D2J234DFA"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/clients/bulk`

##  POST /api/v1/clients/bulk

Bulk actions allow to make changes to multiple clients in a single request the following actions are supported

- archive
- restore
- delete
- template _requires template,template_id properties also_
- assign_group _requires group_settings_id also_
- bulk_update _requires column,new_value also_

All of these actions require an array of client ids to perform the requested action on ie.

"ids":['id1','id2']

actions such as template, assign_group and bulk_update also require additional properties to be passed in the request

- template

The template bulk action allows the creation of a custom template using the provided template_id to be run against the array of clients provided.

- assign_group

Allows setting multiple clients to a single group

- bulk_update

Allows updating certain columns on the client model in bulk. the current list of supported columns that can be updated archived_at:

- public_notes
- industry_id
- size_id
- country_id
- custom_value1
- custom_value2
- custom_value3
- custom_value4


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "archive",
  "ids": [
    "2J234DFA,D2J234DFA,D2J234DFA"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-client-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|body|body|[GenericBulkAction](#schemagenericbulkaction)|true|Bulk action array|
|» action|body|string|false|The action to perform ie. archive / restore / delete|
|» ids|body|[string(string)]|false|none|

## Add client document

<a id="opIduploadClient"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/clients/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=POST' \
  -F 'documents[]=["@/path/to/document.pdf"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/clients/{id}/upload`

##  POST /api/v1/clients/{id}/upload

Handles the uploading of a document to a client, please note due to a quirk in REST you will need to use a _method parameter with value of POST


> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: POST
"documents[]":
  - "@/path/to/document.pdf"
```

<h3 id="add-client-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Client Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents[]|body|[string(binary)]|false|Array of files to upload. The files should be sent with the key name 'documents[]'.<br><br>Supported file types:<br>- PDF (.pdf)<br>- Word (.doc, .docx)<br>- Excel (.xls, .xlsx)<br>- Images (.jpg, .jpeg, .png)<br>- Text (.txt)<br><br>Maximum file size: 20MB per file<br>|

##  POST /api/v1/clients/{id}/purge

Handles purging a client.

> ❗ Note
This is a destructive action.
This action will remove all data associated with the client and cannot be undone.


<h3 id="purge-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|X-API-PASSWORD|header|string|true|The login password when challenged on certain protected routes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Client Hashed ID|

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/clients/D2J234DFA/D2J234DFA/merge \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`POST /api/v1/clients/{id}/{mergeable_client_hashed_id}/merge`

##  POST /api/v1/clients/{id}/{mergeable_client_hashed_id}/merge

Handles merging 2 clients

The id parameter is the client that will be the primary client after the merge has completed. 

The mergeable_client_hashed_id is the client that will be merged into the primary client, this clients records will be updated and associated with the primary client.

> 🚨 **Important**    
This action requires elevated permissions, please note the X-API-PASSWORD header requirements for this route.


<h3 id="merge-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Client statement PDF

<a id="opIdclientStatement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/client_statement \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "start_date": "string",
    "end_date": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "show_payments_table": true,
    "show_credits_table": true,
    "show_aging_table": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/client_statement`

##  POST /api/v1/client_statement

Return a PDF of the client statement

You may also pass the query parameter `?send_email=true` to send the statement via email to the client.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "start_date": "string",
  "end_date": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "show_payments_table": true,
  "show_credits_table": true,
  "show_aging_table": true
}
```

<h3 id="client-statement-pdf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|send_email|query|boolean|false|When set to true, the statement will also be sent via email to the client.|
|body|body|object|true|Statement Options|
|» start_date|body|string|false|The start date of the statement period - format Y-m-d|
|» end_date|body|string|false|The start date of the statement period - format Y-m-d|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The hashed ID of the client|
|» show_payments_table|body|boolean|false|Flag which determines if the payments table is shown|
|» show_credits_table|body|boolean|false|Flag which determines if the credits table is shown|
|» show_aging_table|body|boolean|false|Flag which determines if the aging table is shown|

`POST /api/v1/reactivate_email/{bounce_id}`

##  POST /api/v1/reactivate_email/{bounce_id}

Emails are suppressed by PostMark, when they receive a Hard bounce / Spam Complaint. This endpoint allows you to remove the suppression and send emails to the user again.


<h3 id="removes-email-suppression-of-a-user-in-the-system-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relationships of the Client Object. ie ?include=documents,system_logs<br><br>```html<br>Available includes:<br><br>contacts [All contacts related to the client]<br>documents [All documents related to the client]<br>gateway_tokens [All payment tokens related to the client]<br>activities [All activities related to the client]<br>ledger [The client ledger]<br>system_logs [System logs related to the client]<br>group_settings [The group settings object the client is assigned to]<br><br>```<br><br>Usage:<br><br>```html<br>/api/v1/clients?include=contacts,documents,activities<br>```<br>|
|bounce_id|path|string(string)|true|The postmark Bounce ID reference|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-locations">locations</h1>

The Locations API provides endpoints for managing location records within your company. A location represents a physical
address where you provide services or products to a client OR vendor.


## List locations

<a id="opIdgetLocations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/locations`

##  GET /api/v1/locations

Locations are additional addresses that are applicable to a client. This is useful when a client has multiple addresses for shipping, billing, etc.

When retrieving a list of locations you can chain query parameters to filter the dataset. For example:

```html
/api/v1/locations?name=warehouse*
```

Sorting uses `column|asc` or `column|desc`. Use a single `sort` parameter for one column, or repeated `sort[]` parameters for multi-level ordering (first is primary):

```html
/api/v1/locations?sort=id|desc
/api/v1/locations?sort[]=id|desc&sort[]=name|asc
```

For pagination, use per_page and page parameters:

```html
/api/v1/locations?per_page=15&page=2
```

The default per_page value is 20.


<h3 id="list-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=name\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=name\|asc&sort[]=id\|desc`.<br><br>Location ordering is limited by the filter: `name` is the primary supported case; other column names must exist on the locations schema to take effect.<br>|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by location name<br><br>```html<br>?name=warehouse<br>```<br>|

##  POST /api/v1/locations/bulk

Bulk actions allow to make changes to multiple locations in a single request. The following actions are supported:

- archive
- restore
- delete

All of these actions require an array of location ids to perform the requested action on ie.

"ids":['id1','id2']


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "archive",
  "ids": [
    "2J234DFA,D2J234DFA,D2J234DFA"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-location-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|body|body|[GenericBulkAction](#schemagenericbulkaction)|true|Bulk action array|
|» action|body|string|false|The action to perform ie. archive / restore / delete|
|» ids|body|[string(string)]|false|none|


##  GET /api/v1/products
Lists products within your company.

You can search and filter the result set using query parameters. These can be chained together allowing fine grained lists to be generated.    


<h3 id="list-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=product_key\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=product_key\|asc`.<br><br>Only real columns on the `products` table are recognized (for example `id`, `product_key`, `cost`, `price`). Relationship sorts are not available here. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the entity based on their status. ie active / archived / deleted. Format is a comma separated string with any of the following options:  <br>- active<br>- archived<br>- deleted  <br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?status=archived,deleted<br>Returns only archived and deleted invoices<br>```<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by client_id. Suitable when you only want the entities of a specific client.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?client_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only invoices for the specified client<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by an associated vendor<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/purchases?vendor_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only purchases for the specified vendor<br>```<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Filter by product name|
|product_key|query|string|false|Filter by product key|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

<h3 id="create-product-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|

|» vendor_id|body|string|false|The hashed ID of the vendor that this product is associated with.|

|» in_stock_quantity|body|integer(int32)|false|The quantity of the product that is currently in stock. <br><br>**note** this field is not mutable without passing an extra query parameter which will allow modification of this value.<br><br>The query parameter ?update_in_stock_quantity=true **MUST** be passed if you wish to update this value manually.<br>|

|» income_account_id|body|string|false|The accounting income account identifier this product maps to (used by external accounting integrations such as QuickBooks).|

```json
}
```

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-invoices">invoices</h1>


## Invoice Statuses

- STATUS_DRAFT = 1
  - Draft invoices are not visible in the client portal, are not active and they do not impact the client balance
- STATUS_SENT = 2
  - Send invoices are visible in the client portal, are active and impact the client balance
- STATUS_PARTIAL = 3
  - An invoice which has been partially paid
- STATUS_PAID = 4
  - An invoice which has been fully paid
- STATUS_CANCELLED = 5
  - When a invoice is cancelled the invoice balance is set to zero and the status updated to Cancelled, the client balance is also adjusted down. If payments have been applied to the invoice these will remain linked to the invoice
- STATUS_REVERSED = 6
  - When a invoice has been reversed, the previous payments relationships are unlinked and cannot be restored
- STATUS_OVERDUE = -1
  - An invoice which is still payable past its due date
- STATUS_UNPAID = -2
  - An invoice which is not yet due, but also, not paid

##  GET /api/v1/invoices

Lists invoices with the option to chain multiple query parameters allowing fine grained filtering of the list.  


<h3 id="list-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=balance\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — use `sort[]` for each level in priority order, for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=number\|asc`.<br><br>Invoices accept columns on the `invoices` table, relationship-style keys such as `client.name`, `client_id`, `documents`, `project_id`, and prefixed `client.*` / `contact.*` sorts where the filter supports them. `number` and `status_id` have special handling. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the entity based on their status. ie active / archived / deleted. Format is a comma separated string with any of the following options:  <br>- active<br>- archived<br>- deleted  <br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?status=archived,deleted<br>Returns only archived and deleted invoices<br>```<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by client_id. Suitable when you only want the entities of a specific client.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?client_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only invoices for the specified client<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by an associated vendor<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/purchases?vendor_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only purchases for the specified vendor<br>```<br>|
|client_status|query|string|false|A comma separated list of invoice status strings. Valid options include:  <br>- all<br>- paid  <br>- unpaid  <br>- overdue   <br>|
|number|query|string|false|Search invoices by invoice number <br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Searches across a range of columns including:  <br>- number  <br>- po_number  <br>- date  <br>- amount  <br>- balance  <br>- custom_value1  <br>- custom_value2  <br>- custom_value3  <br>- custom_value4<br>- client.name<br>- client.contacts.[first_name, last_name, email]<br>- line_items.[product_key, notes]<br>|
|without_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Returns the invoice list without the invoices of deleted clients.<br>|
|overdue|query|string|false|Returns the list of invoices that are overdue<br>|
|payable|query|string|false|Returns the invoice list that are payable for a defined client. Please note, you must pass the client_id as the value for this query parameter<br>|
|private_notes|query|string|false|Searches on the private_notes field of the invoices<br>|
|date|query|string|false|Filters the invoices by invoice date returns a list of invoices after (and including) the date<br>|
|date_range|query|string|false|Filters the invoices by invoice date returns a list of invoices between two dates<br>|
|status_id|query|integer|false|Filters the invoices by status id<br><br>```html<br>  STATUS_DRAFT = 1;<br>  STATUS_SENT = 2;<br>  STATUS_PARTIAL = 3;<br>  STATUS_PAID = 4;<br>  STATUS_CANCELLED = 5;<br>  STATUS_REVERSED = 6;<br>```<br>|

## POST /api/v1/invoices
Creates an invoice for a client.

Triggered actions are available when updating or creating an invoice.

These are query parameters that can be chained in order to perform additional actions on the entity, these include:

  ```
  ?send_email=true [Saves and sends the invoice]
  ?mark_sent=true [Saves and marks the invoice as sent]
  ?paid=true [Saves and marks the invoice as paid]
  ?amount_paid=100 [Saves and marks the invoice as paid with the given amount]
  ?cancel=true [Saves and marks the invoice as cancelled]
  ?save_default_footer=true [Saves the current footer as the default footer]
  ?save_default_terms=true [Saves the current terms as the default terms]
  ?retry_e_send=true [Saves and retries the e-send for the invoice]
  ?redirect=https://example.com [Saves and redirects to the given url]
  ```


`PUT /api/v1/invoices/{id}`

## PUT /api/v1/invoices/{id}
Handles the updating of an invoice by id.

Triggered actions are available when updating or creating an invoice.  
These are query parameters that can be chained in order to perform additional actions on the entity, these include:

  ```
  ?send_email=true [Saves and sends the invoice]
  ?mark_sent=true [Saves and marks the invoice as sent]
  ?paid=true [Saves and marks the invoice as paid]
  ?amount_paid=100 [Saves and marks the invoice as paid with the given amount]
  ?cancel=true [Saves and marks the invoice as cancelled]
  ?save_default_footer=true [Saves the current footer as the default footer]
  ?save_default_terms=true [Saves the current terms as the default terms]
  ?retry_e_send=true [Saves and retries the e-send for the invoice]
  ?redirect=https://example.com [Saves and redirects to the given url]
  ```


<h3 id="update-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Invoice Hashed ID|

## Bulk invoice actions

<a id="opIdbulkInvoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/invoices/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "action": "bulk_download",
    "ids": [
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/invoices/bulk`

## POST /api/v1/invoices/bulk

There are multiple actions that are available including:  


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "bulk_download",
  "ids": [
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-invoice-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Bulk action details|
|» email_type|body|string|false|The email type to be sent, when bulk emailing invoices options include:<br>- `invoice` (default)<br>- `quote`<br>- `credit`<br>- `payment`<br>- `payment_partial`<br>- `statement`<br>- `reminder1`<br>- `reminder2`<br>- `reminder3`<br>- `reminder_endless`<br>- `custom1`<br>- `custom2`<br>- `custom3`<br>- `purchase_order`<br>- `email_quote_template_reminder1`<br>|
|» action|body|string|false|The action to be performed, options include:  <br>- `bulk_download`  <br>  Bulk download an array of invoice PDFs (These are sent to the admin via email.)  <br>- `download`  <br>  Download a single PDF. (Returns a single PDF object)  <br>- `bulk_print`  <br>  Merges an array of Invoice PDFs for easy one click printing.  <br>- `auto_bill`  <br>  Attempts to automatically bill the invoices with the payment method on file.  <br>- `clone_to_invoice`  <br>  Returns a clone of the invoice.  <br>- `clone_to_quote`  <br>  Returns a quote cloned using the properties of the given invoice.  <br>- `mark_paid`  <br>  Marks an array of invoices as paid.  <br>- `mark_sent`  <br>  Marks an array of invoices as sent.  <br>- `restore`  <br>  Restores an array of invoices  <br>- `delete`  <br>  Deletes an array of invoices  <br>- `archive`  <br>  Archives an array of invoices  <br>- `cancel`  <br>  Cancels an array of invoices  <br>- `email`  <br>  Emails an array of invoices  <br>- `send_email`  <br>  Emails an array of invoices. Requires additional properties to be sent. `email_type`  <br>|
|» ids|body|[string]|false|none|

```json
{
  "message": "These credentials do not match our records / Invalid Token"
}
```

```json
    ]
  }
```

## Custom invoice action

<a id="opIdactionInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/invoices/D2J234DFA/clone_to_quote \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/invoices/{id}/{action}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Performs a custom action on an invoice.  
The current range of actions are as follows  
- clone_to_invoice  
- clone_to_quote  
- history  
- delivery_note  
- mark_paid  
- download  
- archive  
- delete  
- email

|id|path|string(string)|true|The Invoice Hashed ID|
|action|path|string(string)|true|The action string to be performed|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-recurring-invoices">Recurring Invoices</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with recurring_invoices.


## List recurring invoices

<a id="opIdgetRecurringInvoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_invoices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/recurring_invoices`

## GET /api/v1/recurring_invoices

Lists invoices with the option to chain multiple query parameters allowing fine grained filtering of the list.  


<h3 id="list-recurring-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=next_send_date\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=number\|asc`.<br><br>Recurring invoices use the recurring-invoice table columns plus the client/contact-style sorts exposed by `RecurringInvoiceFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by client_id. Suitable when you only want the entities of a specific client.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?client_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only invoices for the specified client<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by an associated vendor<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/purchases?vendor_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only purchases for the specified vendor<br>```<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Searches across a range of columns including:  <br>- custom_value1  <br>- custom_value2  <br>- custom_value3  <br>- custom_value4<br>|
|client_status|query|string|false|A comma separated list of invoice status strings. Valid options include:  <br>- all<br>- active  <br>- paused  <br>- completed  <br>|
|number|query|string|false|Filters the list by number.<br>|
|product_key|query|string|false|Filters the list by product_key.<br>|
|next_send_between|query|string|false|Filters the list by next_send_between.<br>|
|frequency_id|query|string|false|Filters the list by frequency_id.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


<h3 id="create-recurring-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|body|body|[RecurringInvoiceRequest](#schemarecurringinvoicerequest)|true|Recurring invoice object that needs to be added to the company|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The hashed ID of the client|
|» date|body|string(date)|true|Recurring invoice date|
|» due_date|body|string(date)|true|Due date for the recurring invoice|
|» frequency_id|body|string|true|Frequency ID for recurring invoice|
|» remaining_cycles|body|string|false|Number of remaining cycles|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Private notes for the recurring invoice|
|» public_notes|body|string|false|Public notes for the recurring invoice|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|Custom field value 1|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|Custom field value 2|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|Custom field value 3|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|Custom field value 4|
|» line_items|body|[[InvoiceItem](#schemainvoiceitem)]|false|An array of objects which define the line items of the invoice|

<h3 id="show-recurring-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the RecurringInvoice object|[RecurringInvoice](#schemarecurringinvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update recurring invoice

<a id="opIdupdateRecurringInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_invoices/D2J234DFA \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`PUT /api/v1/recurring_invoices/{id}`

Handles the updating of an RecurringInvoice by id

<h3 id="update-recurring-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The RecurringInvoice Hashed ID|

<h3 id="blank-recurring-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A blank RecurringInvoice object|[RecurringInvoice](#schemarecurringinvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Bulk recurring invoice actions

<a id="opIdbulkRecurringInvoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_invoices/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "action": "start",
    "ids": [
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/recurring_invoices/bulk`

There are multiple actions that are available including:


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "start",
  "ids": [
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-recurring-invoice-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Bulk action details|
|» action|body|string|false|The action to be performed, options include:  <br>- `start`  <br>  Starts (or restarts) the recurring invoice. **note** if the recurring invoice has been stopped for a long time, it will attempt to catch back up firing a new Invoice every hour per interval that has been missed.  <br>  If you do not wish to have the recurring invoice catch up, you should set the next_send_date to the correct date you wish the recurring invoice to commence from.<br>- `stop`  <br>  Stops the recurring invoice. <br>- `send_now`  <br>  Force sends the recurring invoice - this option is only available when the recurring invoice is in a draft state.  <br>- `restore`  <br>  Restores the recurring invoice from an archived or deleted state.<br>- `archive`  <br>  Archives the recurring invoice. The recurring invoice will not fire in this state.<br>- `delete`  <br>  Deletes a recurring invoice.  <br>|
|» ids|body|[string]|false|none|

|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Custom recurring invoice action

<a id="opIdactionRecurringInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_invoices/D2J234DFA/clone_to_quote \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/recurring_invoices/{id}/{action}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Performs a custom action on an RecurringInvoice.

    The current range of actions are as follows
    - clone_to_RecurringInvoice
    - clone_to_quote
    - history
    - delivery_note
    - mark_paid
    - download
    - archive
    - delete
    - email

<h3 id="custom-recurring-invoice-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The RecurringInvoice Hashed ID|
|action|path|string(string)|true|The action string to be performed|

## Add recurring invoice document

<a id="opIduploadRecurringInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_invoices/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/recurring_invoices/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a recurring_invoice

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The RecurringInvoice Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-payments">payments</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with payments.


## List payments

<a id="opIdgetPayments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/payments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/payments`

Lists payments, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

        Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the payments, these are handled by the PaymentFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-payments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=amount\|asc`.<br><br>Payments accept `payments` columns plus client, contact, and document-related sorts defined in the payment filters. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the entity based on their status. ie active / archived / deleted. Format is a comma separated string with any of the following options:  <br>- active<br>- archived<br>- deleted  <br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?status=archived,deleted<br>Returns only archived and deleted invoices<br>```<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by client_id. Suitable when you only want the entities of a specific client.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?client_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only invoices for the specified client<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by an associated vendor<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/purchases?vendor_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only purchases for the specified vendor<br>```<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Searches across a range of columns including:  <br>- amount  <br>- date  <br>- custom_value1  <br>- custom_value2  <br>- custom_value3  <br>- custom_value4<br>|
|number|query|string|false|Search payments by payment number <br>|
