## Create payment

<a id="opIdstorePayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/payments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
    "client_contact_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
    "user_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
    "type_id": "1",
    "date": "2024-01-01",
    "transaction_reference": "xcsSxcs124asd",
    "assigned_user_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
    "private_notes": "The payment was refunded due to error",
    "amount": 10,
    "invoices": [
      {
        "invoice_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
        "amount": "2"
      }
    ],
    "credits": [
      {
        "credit_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
        "amount": "2"
      }
    ],
    "number": "PAY_101"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/payments`

Adds an Payment to the system

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
  "client_contact_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
  "user_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
  "type_id": "1",

  ],
  "credits": [
    {
      "credit_id": "Opnel5aKBz",
      "amount": "2"
    }
  ],
  "number": "PAY_101"
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|email_receipt|query|boolean|false|If true, the payment will be emailed to the client. If false, no email will be sent. This will override any other email settings for payments.<br>|
|body|body|[PaymentRequest](#schemapaymentrequest)|true|The payment request can be as simple as a client id and amount, or as complex as a full payment with invoices and associated credits that should be applied.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The client hashed id|
|» client_contact_id|body|string|false|The client contact hashed id|
|» user_id|body|string|false|The user hashed id|
|» type_id|body|[PaymentType](#schemapaymenttype)|false|The payment type used to complete this payment|
|» date|body|string(date)|false|The Payment date|
|» transaction_reference|body|string|false|The transaction reference as defined by the payment gateway|
|» assigned_user_id|body|string|false|The assigned user hashed id|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|The private notes of the payment|
|» amount|body|number|false|The amount of this payment|
|» invoices|body|[[InvoicePaymentable](#schemainvoicepaymentable)]|false|none|
|» credits|body|[[CreditPaymentable](#schemacreditpaymentable)]|false|none|
|» number|body|string|false|The payment number - is a unique alpha numeric number per payment per company|

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes \

```

`GET /api/v1/quotes`

## GET /api/v1/quotes

Lists quotes, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the quotes, these are handled by the QuoteFilters class which defines the methods available


<h3 id="list-quotes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=number\|asc`.<br><br>Quotes follow the same style as invoices: base `quotes` columns plus `client.name`, `client_id`, `documents`, and `client.*` / `contact.*` where implemented. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the entity based on their status. ie active / archived / deleted. Format is a comma separated string with any of the following options:  <br>- active<br>- archived<br>- deleted  <br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?status=archived,deleted<br>Returns only archived and deleted invoices<br>```<br>|
|client_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by client_id. Suitable when you only want the entities of a specific client.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?client_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only invoices for the specified client<br>```<br>|
|created_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the created at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?created_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities created on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|updated_at|query|integer|false|Filters the entity list by the updated at timestamp. Parameter value can be a datetime string or unix timestamp<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?updated_at=2022-01-10<br>Returns entities last updated on January 10th, 2022<br>```<br>|
|is_deleted|query|boolean|false|Filters the entity list by entities that have been deleted.<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?is_deleted=true<br>Returns only soft-deleted entities<br>```<br>|
|filter_deleted_clients|query|string|false|Filters the entity list and only returns entities for clients that have not been deleted<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/invoices?filter_deleted_clients=true<br>Returns only invoices for active (non-deleted) clients<br>```<br>|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters the entity list by an associated vendor<br><br>```html<br>GET /api/v1/purchases?vendor_id=AxB7Hjk9<br>Returns only purchases for the specified vendor<br>```<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Searches across a range of columns including:  <br>- number  <br>- custom_value1  <br>- custom_value2  <br>- custom_value3  <br>- custom_value4<br>|
|client_status|query|string|false|A comma separated list of quote status strings. Valid options include:  <br>- all<br>- draft  <br>- sent  <br>- approved<br>- expired<br>- upcoming   <br>|
|number|query|string|false|Search quote by quote number <br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "Opnel5aKBz",
```

<h3 id="list-quotes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A list of quotes|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-quotes-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[Quote](#schemaquote)]|false|none|none|
|meta|[Meta](#schemameta)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

`POST /api/v1/quotes`

## POST /api/v1/quotes
Creates an quote for a client.

Triggered actions are available when updating or creating an quote.

These are query parameters that can be chained in order to perform additional actions on the entity, these include:

```
?send_email=true [Saves and sends the quote]
?mark_sent=true [Saves and marks the quote as sent]
?approve=true [Saves and approves the quote]
?convert=true [Saves and converts the quote to an invoice]
?save_default_footer=true [Saves the current footer as the default footer]
?save_default_terms=true [Saves the current terms as the default terms]

```

<h3 id="create-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|body|body|[QuoteRequest](#schemaquoterequest)|true|Quote object that needs to be added to the company|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The hashed ID of the client|
|» date|body|string(date)|true|Quote date|
|» due_date|body|string(date)|true|Due date for the quote|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Private notes for the quote|
|» public_notes|body|string|false|Public notes for the quote|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|Custom field value 1|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|Custom field value 2|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|Custom field value 3|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|Custom field value 4|
|» line_items|body|[[InvoiceItem](#schemainvoiceitem)]|false|An array of objects which define the line items of the quote|

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes/D2J234DFA \

```

`GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}`

## GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}

Displays an Quote by id


<h3 id="show-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Quote Hashed ID|

`PUT /api/v1/quotes/{id}`

## PUT /api/v1/quotes/{id}

Handles the updating of an Quote by id.

Triggered actions are available when updating or creating an quote.

These are query parameters that can be chained in order to perform additional actions on the entity, these include:

```
?send_email=true [Saves and sends the quote]
?mark_sent=true [Saves and marks the quote as sent]
?approve=true [Saves and approves the quote]
?convert=true [Saves and converts the quote to an invoice]
?save_default_footer=true [Saves the current footer as the default footer]
?save_default_terms=true [Saves the current terms as the default terms]

```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Quote Hashed ID|
|body|body|[QuoteRequest](#schemaquoterequest)|true|Quote object that needs to be updated|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The hashed ID of the client|
|» date|body|string(date)|true|Quote date|
|» due_date|body|string(date)|true|Due date for the quote|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Private notes for the quote|
|» public_notes|body|string|false|Public notes for the quote|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|Custom field value 1|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|Custom field value 2|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|Custom field value 3|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|Custom field value 4|
|» line_items|body|[[InvoiceItem](#schemainvoiceitem)]|false|An array of objects which define the line items of the quote|

<h3 id="edit-quote-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the Quote object|[Quote](#schemaquote)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes/create \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/quotes/create`

## GET /api/v1/quotes/create

Returns a blank object with default values


<h3 id="blank-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|

## Bulk quote actions

<a id="opIdbulkQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "action": "convert",
    "ids": [
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA",
      "D2J234DFA"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/quotes/bulk`

## POST /api/v1/quotes/bulk

Performs bulk actions on an array of quotes


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "convert",
  "ids": [
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA",
    "D2J234DFA"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-quote-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Bulk action details|
|» action|body|string|false|The action to be performed, options include:  <br>- `approve`  <br>  Bulk approve an array of quotes  <br>- `convert`  <br>  Bulk convert an array of quotes to invoices  <br>- `send_email`  <br>  Bulk send an array of quotes as emails  <br>- `mark_sent`  <br>  Bulk mark an array of quotes as sent  <br>- `restore`  <br>  Restores an array of quotes  <br>- `delete`  <br>  Deletes an array of invoices  <br>- `archive`  <br>  Archives an array of invoices  <br>|
|» ids|body|[string]|false|none|

## Performs a custom action on an Quote

<a id="opIdactionQuote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes/D2J234DFA/clone_to_quote \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}/{action}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Performs a custom action on an Quote.

    The current range of actions are as follows
    - clone_to_quote
    - history
    - delivery_note
    - mark_paid
    - download
    - archive
    - delete
    - convert
    - convert_to_invoice
    - email

<h3 id="performs-a-custom-action-on-an-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Quote Hashed ID|
|action|path|string(string)|true|The action string to be performed|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/quote/{invitation_key}/download`

## Upload a quote document

<a id="opIduploadQuote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/quotes/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/quotes/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a quote

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

<h3 id="upload-a-quote-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Quote Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-credits">credits</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with credits.


## List credits

<a id="opIdgetCredits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/credits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/credits`

Lists credits, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.
     *
     *      Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the credits, these are handled by the CreditFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-credits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=balance\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=number\|asc&sort[]=date\|desc`.<br><br>Credits accept credit table columns plus `client.name`, `client_id`, `documents`, and `client.*` / `contact.*` style keys per `CreditFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

|» invitations|body|[[CreditInvitationRequest](#schemacreditinvitationrequest)]|false|An array of objects which define the invitations of the credit|
|» discount|body|number(float)|false|The credit discount, can be an amount or a percentage|
|» partial|body|number(float)|false|The deposit/partial amount|
|» is_amount_discount|body|boolean|false|Flag determining if the discount is an amount or a percentage|

|» date|body|string(date)|false|The credit Date|
|» partial_due_date|body|string(date)|false|The due date for the deposit/partial amount|
|» due_date|body|string(date)|false|The due date of the credit|

<h3 id="create-credit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the saved credit object|[Credit](#schemacredit)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Show credit

<a id="opIdshowCredit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/credits/D2J234DFA \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/credits/{id}`

Displays an credit by id

<h3 id="show-credit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Credit Hashed ID|

<h3 id="blank-credit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A blank credit object|[Credit](#schemacredit)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '[
    "[D2J234DFA,D2J234DFA,D2J234DFA]"
  ]'
```

```json
[

]
```

## Upload a credit document

<a id="opIduploadCredits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/credits/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/credits/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a credit

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

<h3 id="upload-a-credit-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Credit Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

## List tasks

<a id="opIdgetTasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/tasks`

Lists tasks, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.
     *
     *   Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the tasks, these are handled by the TaskFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=due_date\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=status_id\|asc&sort[]=id\|desc`.<br><br>Tasks accept `tasks` columns plus `client.name`, `client_id`, `contact.*`, and `documents` where the filter implements them. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

## List vendors

<a id="opIdgetVendors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/vendors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/vendors`

Lists vendors, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

    Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the vendors, these are handled by the VendorFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-vendors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=name\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=name\|asc`.<br><br>Vendors use vendor table columns and any relationship sorts implemented in `VendorFilters` (such as `client.name` or document counts where applicable). Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

## Uploads a vendor document

<a id="opIduploadVendor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/vendors/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/vendors/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a vendor

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

<h3 id="uploads-a-vendor-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Vendor Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-purchase-orders">Purchase Orders</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with purchase orders.


## List purchase orders

<a id="opIdgetPurchaseOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/purchase_orders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/purchase_orders`

Lists purchase orders, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.
     *
     *      Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the purchase orders, these are handled by the PurchaseOrderFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-purchase-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=number\|asc&sort[]=date\|desc`.<br><br>Purchase orders use PO table columns and vendor- or client-related sorts as defined in `PurchaseOrderFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

<h3 id="show-purchase-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the purchase order object|[PurchaseOrder](#schemapurchaseorder)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update purchase order

<a id="opIdupdatePurchaseOrder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/purchase_order/D2J234DFA \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "vendor_id": "D2J234DFA",
    "date": "2024-01-01",
    "due_date": "2024-01-31",
    "private_notes": "Internal notes about this purchase order",
    "public_notes": "Please deliver to our warehouse",
    "custom_value1": "Custom value 1",
    "custom_value2": "Custom value 2",

    "custom_value4": "Custom value 4",

        "product_key": "PROD_001",
        "notes": "Office supplies",
        "discount": 0,
        "is_amount_discount": true,
        "tax_name1": "Sales Tax",
        "tax_rate1": 8.5,
        "tax_name2": "",
        "tax_rate2": 0,
        "tax_name3": "",
        "tax_rate3": 0,
```

<h3 id="update-purchase-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The purchase order Hashed ID|
|body|body|[PurchaseOrderRequest](#schemapurchaseorderrequest)|true|Purchase order object that needs to be updated|
|» vendor_id|body|string|true|The hashed ID of the vendor|
|» date|body|string(date)|true|Purchase order date|
|» due_date|body|string(date)|true|Due date for the purchase order|
|» private_notes|body|string|false|Private notes for the purchase order|
|» public_notes|body|string|false|Public notes for the purchase order|
|» custom_value1|body|string|false|Custom field value 1|
|» custom_value2|body|string|false|Custom field value 2|
|» custom_value3|body|string|false|Custom field value 3|
|» custom_value4|body|string|false|Custom field value 4|
|» line_items|body|[object]|false|Array of line items for the purchase order|
|» » quantity|body|number|false|none|
|» » cost|body|number|false|none|
|» » product_key|body|string|false|none|
|» » notes|body|string|false|none|
|» » discount|body|number|false|none|
|» » is_amount_discount|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » tax_name1|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_rate1|body|number|false|none|
|» » tax_name2|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_rate2|body|number|false|none|
|» » tax_name3|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_rate3|body|number|false|none|
|» » sort_id|body|string|false|none|
|» » custom_value1|body|string|false|none|
|» » custom_value2|body|string|false|none|
|» » custom_value3|body|string|false|none|
|» » custom_value4|body|string|false|none|
|» » type_id|body|string|false|none|

`GET /api/v1/purchase_orders/{id}/{action}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Performs a custom action on an purchase order.

<h3 id="custom-purchase-order-actions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the purchase order object|[PurchaseOrder](#schemapurchaseorder)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Uploads a purchase order document

<a id="opIduploadPurchaseOrder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/purchase_orders/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/purchase_orders/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a purchase_order

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

<h3 id="uploads-a-purchase-order-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Purchase Order Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

## Gets a list of expenses

<a id="opIdgetExpenses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/expenses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/expenses`

Lists expenses, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

    Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the expenses, these are handled by the ExpenseFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-expenses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=amount\|asc&sort[]=date\|desc`.<br><br>Expenses accept expense columns plus client, contact, and document-related sorts per `ExpenseFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

## Gets a list of recurring_expenses

<a id="opIdgetRecurringExpenses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_expenses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/recurring_expenses`

Lists recurring_expenses, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

    Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the recurring_expenses, these are handled by the RecurringExpenseFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-recurringexpenses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=next_send_date\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=amount\|desc`.<br><br>Recurring expenses combine table columns with client- or vendor-related sorts from `RecurringExpenseFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

## Gets a list of bank_transactions

<a id="opIdgetBankTransactions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/bank_transactions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/bank_transactions`

Lists all bank integrations

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-banktransactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|rows|query|number(integer)|false|The number of bank integrations to return|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=amount\|asc&sort[]=date\|desc`.<br><br>Bank transactions accept columns and relationship sorts exposed by `BankTransactionFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

> 200 Response

```json
    {
      "id": "AS3df3A",
      "user_id": "AS3df3A",
      "transaction_id": 343434,

      "account_type": "creditCard",
      "description": "Potato purchases for kevin",
      "category_id": 1,
      "category_type": "Expenses",
      "base_type": "CREDIT",
      "date": "2022-09-01",
      "bank_account_id": 1
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
```

## Match transactions

<a id="opIdmatchBankTransactions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/bank_transactions/match \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '[
    0
  ]'
```

`POST /api/v1/bank_transactions/match`

Matching invoices or a payment to a bank transactions.

The API expects the id of the transaction along with either a comma separated list of invoice ids OR the payment id to associate the transaction to.

Example for matching a transaction to two invoices:

{"transactions":[{"id":"olejRl5ejN","invoice_ids":"JxboYBLegw,JxboYBLeXX"}]}

Example for matching a transaction and a paymente:

{"transactions":[{"id":"olejRl5ejN","payment_id":"JxboYBLeXf"}]}

Matching expenses.

You can match an existing expense within Invoice Ninja - or - create a new expense using the following:

{"transactions":[{"id":"open5pld7A","vendor_id":"gl9avJnaG1","ninja_category_id":""}]}

To match to an existing expense:

{"transactions":[{"id":"Jxbo2qKagw","expense_id":"7N1aMM1aWm"}]}


> Body parameter

```json
[
  0
]
```

|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|

|» start_date|body|string|false|The start date to search between|
|» end_date|body|string|false|The end date to search between|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-activities">activities</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with activities.


## Returns a list of activities

<a id="opIdgetActivities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/activities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/activities`

Lists all activities related to this company

<h3 id="returns-a-list-of-activities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Include child relations of the Activity object, format is comma separated. **Note** it is possible to chain multiple includes together, ie. include=account,token|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|

|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=id\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=created_at\|asc`.<br><br>Only columns on `bank_integrations` are recognized. `GET /api/v1/client_gateway_tokens`

Lists client_gateway_tokens, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

    Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the client_gateway_tokens, these are handled by the ClientGatewayTokenFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="list-of-client-payment-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "Opnel5aKBz",
      "client_id": "2",
      "token": "2",
      "routing_number": "2",
      "company_gateway_id": "2",
      "is_default": true
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 1,
      "count": 1,
      "per_page": 1,
      "current_page": 1,
      "total_pages": 1,
      "links": {}
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "message": "These credentials do not match our records / Invalid Token"
```

```json
  "message": "Insufficient permissions for this resource.",

    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
```

```json
{
```

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-companies">companies</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with companies.


## Gets a list of companies

<a id="opIdgetCompanies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/companies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/companies`

Lists companies, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

        Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the companies, these are handled by the CompanyFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-companies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|

```json
{
```

```json
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded.",
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "message": "Unexpected error",
  "code": 500
}
```

<h3 id="adds-a-company-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the saved company object|[Company](#schemacompany)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Gets a new blank company object

<a id="opIdgetCompaniesCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/companies/create \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/companies/create`

Returns a blank object with default values

<h3 id="gets-a-new-blank-company-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|

<h3 id="updates-an-company-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the company object|[Company](#schemacompany)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Deletes a company

<a id="opIddeleteCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/companies/D2J234DFA \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/companies/{id}`

Handles the deletion of an company by id

<h3 id="deletes-a-company-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Company Hashed ID|

> Example responses

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

## Uploads a document to a company

<a id="opIduploadCompanies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/companies/D2J234DFA/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F '_method=PUT' \
  -F 'documents=["string"]'
```

`POST /api/v1/companies/{id}/upload`

Handles the uploading of a document to a company

> Body parameter

```yaml
_method: PUT
documents:
  - string
```

<h3 id="uploads-a-document-to-a-company-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The Company Hashed ID|
|body|body|object|true|File Upload Body|
|» _method|body|string|false|none|
|» documents|body|[string(binary)]|false|none|

```json

  "message": "The given data was invalid.",
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded.",
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "message": "Unexpected error",
  "code": 500
}
```

<h3 id="sets-the-company-as-the-default-company-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the company object|[Company](#schemacompany)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit Exceeded|[RateLimiterError](#schemaratelimitererror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Server error|None|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Returns the current comapny

<a id="opIdshowCurrentCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/companies/current \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`POST /api/v1/companies/current`

Returns the current company based on the API token passed in

<h3 id="returns-the-current-comapny-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|

## Gets a list of company_gateways

<a id="opIdgetCompanyGateways"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/company_gateways \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/company_gateways`

Lists company_gateways, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

        Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the company_gateways, these are handled by the CompanyGatewayFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-companygateways-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=label\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=label\|asc`.<br><br>Sorting is limited to columns on the company gateways table (for example `label`, `id`). Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-connectedaccount">connected_account</h1>

Endpoint definitions for connecting accounts.


## Connect an oauth user to an existing user

<a id="opIdpostConnectedAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/connected_account \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`POST /api/v1/connected_account`

Refreshes the dataset

<h3 id="connect-an-oauth-user-to-an-existing-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|include_static|query|string|false|This include will return the full set of static variables used in the application including:<br>  - Currencies<br>  - Countries <br>  - Languages<br>  - Payment Types<br>  - Email Templatees<br>  - Industries<br>|
|clear_cache|query|string|false|Clears cache<br><br>Clears (and rebuilds) the static variable cache.  <br>|

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-designs">designs</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with designs.


## Gets a list of designs

<a id="opIdgetDesigns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/designs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/designs`

Lists designs

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-designs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=name\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=name\|asc`.<br><br>Only `designs` table columns apply. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "AS3df3A",
      "name": "Beauty",
      "design": "<html></html>",
      "is_custom": true,
      "is_active": true,
      "is_deleted": true,
      "created_at": 134341234234,
      "updated_at": 134341234234,
      "deleted_at": 134341234234
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 1,
      "count": 1,
      "per_page": 1,
      "current_page": 1,
      "total_pages": 1,
      "links": {}
    }
  }
}
```

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-documents">documents</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with documents.


## Gets a list of documents

<a id="opIdgetDocuments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/documents \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/documents`

Lists documents, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

    Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the documents, these are handled by the DocumentsFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-documents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|index|query|string|false|Replaces the default response index from data to a user specific string<br><br>ie.<br><br>```html<br>  ?index=new_index<br>```<br><br>response is wrapped<br><br>```json<br>  {<br>    'new_index' : [<br>      .....  <br>    ]<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=created_at\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=id\|desc&sort[]=created_at\|asc`.<br><br>Documents accept base table columns and any extra relationship sorts implemented in `DocumentFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "AS3df3A",
      "user_id": "",
      "assigned_user_id": "",
      "project_id": "",
      "vendor_id": "",
      "name": "Beauty",
      "url": "Beauty",
      "preview": "Beauty",
      "type": "Beauty",
      "disk": "Beauty",
      "hash": "Beauty",
      "is_deleted": true,
      "is_default": true,
      "created_at": 134341234234,
      "updated_at": 134341234234,
      "deleted_at": 134341234234
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 1,
      "count": 1,
      "per_page": 1,
      "current_page": 1,
      "total_pages": 1,
      "links": {}
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "These credentials do not match our records / Invalid Token"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Insufficient permissions for this resource.",
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{

  "errors": {

    ]
  }
```

<h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-imports">imports</h1>

Endpoint definitions for pre-import operations.


## Pre Import CSV data

<a id="opIdpreimport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/preimport \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F 'import_type=invoice' \
  -F 'files[invoice]=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'files[client]=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'files[product]=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'files[payment]=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'files[vendor]=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'files[expense]=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /api/v1/preimport`

The preimport endpoint is the first step when importing CSV data into Invoice Ninja. It validates your file(s) and returns the column headers found in each CSV, allowing you to map them to system fields before performing the actual import.

**How it works**

1. Set `import_type` to indicate the entity type (e.g. `invoice`, `quote`, `client`, `product`, `payment`, `vendor`, `expense`).
2. Attach one or more CSV files using the `files[]` parameter, keyed by entity type:
   - `files[invoice]` — invoice records
   - `files[client]` — client records
   - `files[product]` — product records
   - `files[payment]` — payment records
   - `files[vendor]` — vendor records
   - `files[expense]` — expense records
3. The response returns the detected column headers for each uploaded file so you can build a field mapping for the subsequent `/api/v1/import` call.

You may upload multiple entity files in a single request. Only include the entity types relevant to your import.

**Example**

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://invoiceninja.com/api/v1/preimport' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'import_type=invoice' \
  -F 'files[invoice]=@invoices.csv' \
  -F 'files[client]=@clients.csv'
```


> Body parameter

```yaml
import_type: invoice
"files[invoice]": string
"files[client]": string
"files[product]": string
"files[payment]": string
"files[vendor]": string
"files[expense]": string
```

<h3 id="pre-import-csv-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|body|body|object|true|The CSV file(s) and import type|
|» import_type|body|string|true|The type of import being performed|
|» files[invoice]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for invoices|
|» files[client]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for clients|
|» files[product]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for products|
|» files[payment]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for payments|
|» files[vendor]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for vendors|
|» files[expense]|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file for expenses|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "hash": "MvKeSwMnhAfgkzdYKgxM5ummxGbLIdNm",
  "mappings": {
    "property1": {
      "available": [
        "invoice.number",
        "invoice.amount",
        "client.name",
        "item.quantity",
        "item.cost"
      ],
      "headers": [
        [
          "Client Name",
          "Invoice Number",
          "Amount"
        ],
        [
          "Acme Corp",
          "INV-001",
          "1500.00"
        ]
      ],
      "hints": [
        4,
        0,
        2
      ]
    },
    "property2": {
      "available": [
        "invoice.number",
        "invoice.amount",
        "client.name",
        "item.quantity",
        "item.cost"
      ],
      "headers": [
        [
          "Client Name",
          "Invoice Number",
          "Amount"
        ],
        [
          "Acme Corp",
          "INV-001",
          "1500.00"
        ]
      ],
      "hints": [
        4,
        0,
        2
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "These credentials do not match our records / Invalid Token"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Insufficient permissions for this resource.",
  "errors": {
    "value": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="pre-import-csv-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a hash identifying the uploaded file(s) and a mappings object for each entity type submitted.<br><br>- **hash** — A unique reference to the uploaded file(s). Pass this to `/api/v1/import` when executing the import.<br>- **mappings** — An object keyed by entity type (e.g. `invoice`, `client`). Each entity contains:<br>  - **available** — The system fields that can be mapped to for this entity (e.g. `invoice.number`, `client.name`, `item.cost`).<br>  - **headers** — A two-dimensional array. The first element contains the column headers detected from your CSV. The second element contains a sample data row, useful for previewing values during field mapping.<br>  - **hints** — An array of suggested mappings, one per CSV column. Each value is an index into the `available` array representing the best-guess system field for that column, or `null` when no match could be determined.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication error|[AuthenticationError](#schemaauthenticationerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Authorization error|[AuthorizationError](#schemaauthorizationerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error|[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="pre-import-csv-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hash|string|false|none|Unique reference to the uploaded file(s), required for the subsequent import call.|
|mappings|object|false|none|An object keyed by entity type containing field mapping data for each uploaded CSV.|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » available|[string]|false|none|System fields available for mapping.|
|» » headers|[[string]]|false|none|A two-element array: the first element is the CSV column headers, the second is a sample data row.|
|» » hints|[integer \| null]|false|none|Suggested mapping indices into the `available` array for each CSV column. A value of null indicates no suggested match.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-MINIMUM-CLIENT-VERSION|number||The API version|
|200|X-RateLimit-Remaining|integer||The number of requests left for the time window.|
|200|X-RateLimit-Limit|integer||The total number of requests in a given time window.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Import CSV data

<a id="opIdpostImport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -d '{
    "hash": "MvKeSwMnhAfgkzdYKgxM5ummxGbLIdNm",
    "import_type": "csv",
    "skip_header": true,
    "column_map": {
      "property1": {
        "mapping": {
          "0": "client.name",
          "1": "client.email",
          "2": "",
          "3": "invoice.number",
          "4": "invoice.amount"
        }
      },
      "property2": {
        "mapping": {
          "0": "client.name",
          "1": "client.email",
          "2": "",
          "3": "invoice.number",
          "4": "invoice.amount"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/import`

The import endpoint executes the actual data import. Call this after `/api/v1/preimport` has returned the file hash, available fields, and column headers.

Using the data from the preimport response, construct a `column_map` that tells the system how each CSV column maps to a system field. The import runs asynchronously — you will receive an email notification once it completes.

**Request body**

- **hash** — The unique file reference returned by `/api/v1/preimport`.
- **import_type** — The source format (e.g. `csv`, `freshbooks`, `invoice2go`, `invoicely`).
- **skip_header** — Set to `true` to skip the first row of the CSV (the header row).
- **column_map** — An object keyed by entity type (e.g. `invoice`, `client`). Each entity contains:
  - **mapping** — An object where each key is the CSV column index (as a string) and each value is the target system field from the `available` array, or an empty string `""` to skip that column.

---

### Available mapping fields

Each mapping value uses the format `entity.property`. The tables below list every available field per entity type.

### Data Matching:

#### Client Matching:
  Matching a record to a client is performed by using the clients email address (first) or the clients (exact) name. If no match is found, a new client is created.

#### Multi line item invoice/quote/credits/recurring invoice Matching:
  If you need to import multiple line items into an invoice (other other entity) you will want to assign the same (unique) invoice number to each row in the csv file, the system will group together lines where the invoice number is the same and create line items for each row.

| `invoice.remaining_cycles` | Remaining billing cycles |
| `invoice.auto_bill` | Auto-bill setting |
| `invoice.next_send_date` | Next send date (replaces `invoice.date`) |

#### Task fields (`files[task]`)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `task.number` | Task number |
| `task.user_id` | Assigned user |
| `task.rate` | Hourly rate |
| `task.description` | Task description |
| `task.billable` | Whether the task is billable |
| `task.status` | Task status |
| `task.start_date` | Start date |
| `task.end_date` | End date |
| `task.start_time` | Start time |
| `task.end_time` | End time |
| `task.duration` | Duration |
| `task.custom_value1` | Custom field 1 |
| `task.custom_value2` | Custom field 2 |
| `task.custom_value3` | Custom field 3 |
| `task.custom_value4` | Custom field 4 |
| `task.notes` | Task notes |
| `project.name` | Project name |
| `client.name` | Client name |
| `client.email` | Client email |

#### Bank transaction fields (`files[bank_transaction]`)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `transaction.transaction_id` | Transaction ID |
| `transaction.amount` | Transaction amount |
| `transaction.currency` | Currency |
| `transaction.account_type` | Account type |
| `transaction.category` | Category |
| `transaction.category_type` | Category type |
| `transaction.date` | Transaction date |
| `transaction.bank_account` | Bank account |
| `transaction.description` | Description |
| `transaction.base_type` | Base type |
| `transaction.payment_type_Credit` | Credit amount |
| `transaction.payment_type_Debit` | Debit amount |
| `transaction.participant` | Participant reference |
| `transaction.participant_name` | Participant name |

---

**Example**

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://invoiceninja.com/api/v1/import' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "hash": "MvKeSwMnhAfgkzdYKgxM5ummxGbLIdNm",
    "import_type": "csv",
    "skip_header": true,
    "column_map": {
      "invoice": {
        "mapping": {
          "0": "client.name",
          "1": "client.email",
          "2": "",
          "3": "invoice.number",
          "4": "invoice.amount"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "hash": "MvKeSwMnhAfgkzdYKgxM5ummxGbLIdNm",
  "import_type": "csv",
  "skip_header": true,
  "column_map": {
    "property1": {
      "mapping": {
        "0": "client.name",
        "1": "client.email",
        "2": "",
        "3": "invoice.number",
        "4": "invoice.amount"
      }
    },
    "property2": {
      "mapping": {
        "0": "client.name",
        "1": "client.email",
        "2": "",
        "3": "invoice.number",
        "4": "invoice.amount"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|body|body|object|true|The column mapping and file reference for the import|
|» hash|body|string|true|The unique file reference returned by the preimport endpoint.|
|» import_type|body|string|true|The source format of the import.|
|» skip_header|body|boolean|false|When true, the first row of the CSV is treated as a header row and skipped during import.|
|» column_map|body|object|true|An object keyed by entity type. Each entity contains a mapping of CSV column indices to system fields.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » mapping|body|object|false|Maps CSV column indices (as string keys) to system field names from the `available` array. Use an empty string to skip a column.|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=number_of_days\|asc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=name\|asc&sort[]=number_of_days\|asc`.<br><br>Sorting follows the payment term table schema. <h1 id="invoice-ninja-api-reference-recurringquotes">recurring_quotes</h1>

Endpoint definitions for interacting with recurring quotes.


## Gets a list of recurring_quotes

<a id="opIdgetRecurringQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://invoicing.co/api/v1/recurring_quotes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-API-TOKEN: TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest'
```

`GET /api/v1/recurring_quotes`

Lists recurring_quotes, search and filters allow fine grained lists to be generated.

        Query parameters can be added to performed more fine grained filtering of the recurring_quotes, these are handled by the RecurringQuoteFilters class which defines the methods available

<h3 id="gets-a-list-of-recurringquotes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-API-TOKEN|header|string|true|The API token to be used for authentication|
|X-Requested-With|header|string|true|Used to send the XMLHttpRequest header|
|include|query|string|false|Includes child relationships in the response, format is comma separated. Check each model for the list of associated includes|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return for each request, default is 20|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number to return for this request (when performing pagination), default is 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Order the list by choosing a column and direction. Each value uses the form `column\|asc` or `column\|desc`.<br><br>**Single sort** — for example `sort=next_send_date\|desc`.<br><br>**Multiple sorts** — for example  <br>`sort[]=number\|asc&sort[]=id\|desc`.<br><br>Recurring quotes use their table columns and related sorts from `RecurringQuoteFilters`. Unsupported keys are ignored.<br>|
